{{Short description|Infinite binary tree}}
{{for|the surface|Cantor tree surface}}
In mathematical set theory, the '''Cantor tree''' is either the full [[binary tree]] of height ω&nbsp;+&nbsp;1, or a [[topological space]] related to this by joining its points with intervals.

It was introduced by [[Robert Lee Moore]] in the late 1920s as an example of a non-metrizable [[Moore space (topology)|Moore space]] {{harv|Jones|1966}}.
